title: Visit to Boston made Boca Raton resident feel miserable about living in Boca Raton
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Ian Pinto, 20, from Boca Raton, felt inspired after a four-day visit to Boston.
Pinto appreciated Boston's walkability, public transportation, and comparatively lower prices.
He noted Boston's welcoming atmosphere and hopes to move there in the future.

title: Motorcyclist killed in crash with pickup truck in Raynham
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Jason Marshall, 31, of Taunton, died in a motorcycle crash at Route 138 and Elm Street in Raynham.
The crash involved Marshall's Suzuki TL 1000 motorcycle and a 2015 Chevy Silverado, driven by a 57-year-old man.
State Police and Raynham police are investigating the incident; the truck driver remained on scene and cooperated.

title: N.H. police seek to identify suspects who fatally shot dog in attempted armed robbery
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A dog was killed during an attempted armed robbery early Tuesday in Hollis, New Hampshire.
A man and woman displayed a firearm and demanded money from the victim, police reported.
Hollis police urge locals to review security footage to help identify the suspects involved.

title: Former Red Sox infielder criticized front office: ‘Some people watch the game, some people go on the computer’
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Vaughn Grissom criticized the Red Sox's reliance on analytics, blaming it for lack of belief in him as a player.
Traded to the Angels for a minor-league prospect, Grissom improved his performance, batting .254 in 2026.
Grissom expressed no hard feelings towards Red Sox teammates, but wished for more opportunity to prove himself.

title: Authorities investigating 4 family members shot in N.H. as potential attempted murders and suicide
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 29-year-old man died by suicide after a shooting incident involving four family members in Whitefield, New Hampshire.
Amy Blake, 59, and Michael Marro, 41, are in critical condition; Eric Blake Sr., 53, is stable after a shooting.
Authorities are treating the case as a potential attempted murder-suicide with no threat to the general public.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues with her psychiatric treatment in the spotlight
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Lindsay Clancy's murder trial focuses on her psychiatric treatment and alleged postpartum mental illness defense.
Massachusetts State Police Sgt. Daniel Lawlor testified about the involvement of a forensic psychologist at Brigham and Women's Hospital.
Clancy is charged with the murder of her three children during an episode of postpartum mental illness on January 24, 2023.

title: Acton teen located after police discover two dead in home
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: A woman and teenage boy were found dead in their Acton home on Martha Lane.
17-year-old resident Arjun Aravind was located after being sought in connection with the case.
A 2014 green Honda Accord linked to the case was found in Wayland; investigation is ongoing.

title: Q&A: Boston’s nightlife czar says the city is just getting started
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Boston's nightlife strategy includes extended bar hours and social districts to boost a 24-hour economy.
Director Corean Reynolds reported increased revenue for businesses and no complaints during this summer's social district pilots.
Future plans aim to further relax alcohol regulations, improve late-night transport, and expand nightlife options citywide.

title: Recent homes sales in Greater Boston (Aug. 12)
author: The Boston Globe
bullets: Abington: 416 Thayer St. #416 sold for $437,000; 1,334 sq ft, 2 bedrooms, 2 baths.
Acton: 16 Chestnut St. #5 condo sold for $1,190,000; 3 bedrooms, 3 baths.
Boston: 46 Beacon St. #Ph8 condo sold for $18,000,000; highest sale in the city.

title: Nearly 50 children recovered during anti-human trafficking operation in Greater Boston during the World Cup, officials say
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Operation Yellow Card recovered 48 missing and endangered children aged 12-17 in Greater Boston during the World Cup.
The multi-agency operation involved the U.S. Marshals, Massachusetts State Police, and Boston Police Department.
Investigations continue into child exploitation, kidnapping, and human trafficking following the recovery of the children.
